cohort: Women of reproductive age undergoing transcervical resection of the septum (TCRS) for either incomplete or complete uterine septa.
finding: TCRS significantly decreased spontaneous abortion and embryonic arrest rates while increasing pregnancy and full-term birth rates in women with uterine septa, though it also led to a rise in cesarean section rates.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates increased overall and were significantly higher in patients with complete uterine septum compared to those with incomplete uterine septum following TCRS.
